rationale: Ground truth has no substantive concerns (just approvals), so recall is vacuously satisfied by both. X's findings are all minor/nit-tier doc-consistency polish with ready-to-apply GitHub suggestion blocks, giving it an actionability edge. Y goes deeper, tracing the actual code path to show the PR's new 'returns silent audio' claim is likely wrong (the traced chain produces a 500 error, not a zero-amplitude WAV) — a genuine correctness catch on added text, not a nit — and also correctly scopes the overbroad 'curl doesn't flatten extra_body' claim against a counter-example (GLM-Image recipe), while X's parallel README-staleness finding is a weaker, more superficial catch that Y explicitly investigates and dismisses as a non-issue. Y's superior grounding and value on the highest-severity finding outweighs X's cleaner suggestion-diff formatting.
